newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac sees budget pact deal in Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac sees budget pact deal in Amsterdam.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Tuesday he hoped a stability pact limiting budget deficits of countries that join a single European currency could be agreed at a summit in Amsterdam next week.

Speaking a day after France's new Socialist-led government requested a delay to study the stability pact, both Chirac and Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said they were optimistic that the summit would also be able to conclude negotiations on reforming European Union institutions.
After talks in Paris, Kok told reporters that all EU countries sought a Europe which was not just monetarist but also focused on jobs.
"It is important to see how one can develop an additional element on top of the stability pact" to promote employment, he said.
The conservative Chirac gave his backing to the left-wing government, saying it was right to stress employment.

Kok said he hoped it would be possible to have "good preparations" on the stability pact before Amsterdam, but he added "there is no guarantee". French European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici said on Monday he did not believe the pact could be approved at the summit on June 16 and 17.
Chirac told reporters he and Kok had discussed preparations for the Amsterdam summit, which the Dutch leader will chair. He reaffirmed France's determination to launch the single currency on time.
"France is committed to launching the euro on January 1, 1999," he said. "This assumes that we look in Amsterdam at the stability pact, which I hope can be concluded in Amsterdam."
He noted that France had always pushed for greater emphasis on jobs in Europe which the new French government had just stressed "quite rightly".
EU ministers and officials are to hold intensive negotiations this week to try to reach an agreement in time for the Amsterdam summit.
"I hope it will be possible to have a good preparation before Amsterdam on the stability pact," Kok said.
He said the French government was not alone in wanting to stress jobs.

Chirac and Kok both voiced optimism about the conclusion of the EU's intergovernmental conference (IGC), which some analysts had suggested might be put at risk because of the row over the stability pact.
"I think that we should have a positive result (on the IGC) in Amsterdam," Chirac said.
On the same issue, Kok said: "I am optimistic about the possibility of completing negotiations in Amsterdam."
